rows.grounds: locative of locus; refers to śakti as the seat or presence
ritual act of summoning a deity
negates the existence or applicability of invocation
introduces the reason for the absence of invocation
subject identified as the deity herself
compound indicating she is inherently present in her own form

items.question: Why is ritual invocation inapplicable when the goddess is inherently present as power?
premises: Invocation presupposes the deity's absence from the locus.
The goddess is present in her own essential nature.
Power is the locus where her presence is already established.
items.inference: Because the goddess is inherently present as power, no act of invocation is required.
uncertainties: The precise referent of śaktau may depend on the ritual configuration described in the preceding verses.
items.plain_english: There is no invocation in the power, because the goddess is present in her own essential form.
